text:
Concerning Experience with this candy:
i decided to try these out.. they tasted amazing actually. I loved them. But a few hours after eating them i started feeling weird. 
It was after a long shift at work so i didnt eat anything that day, so it definitely wasnt food poisoning from other food.

But, im not even joking this candy gave me the most violent diarrhea ive ever experienced, i was using the stool urgently like every 5-10 mins until i ran out of liquid. It spewed out of me like water. It felt like i took laxatives on steroids.
This candy left me severely dehydrated because of that. I had to call out of work the next day because of how dehydrated i was. 

The crazy thing is i was curious about it so i researched the candy and its just not me. Loads of other people have shared my experience.
I've tried emailing the company to inform them about what happened but they didnt even respond. 

All i have to say is eat this candy at your own risk.

text: Hey Ryan, I went to A&M last semester too. I guess you can say it's my own fault for letting stuff get to me, but I regret not having kept improving my time and reaching out to those college coaches. I'm sure if would have, my life would've looked a lot better than it does now. Today, I'm busting my ass, trying to make a name for myself in the running world and trying to improve my gpa at comm college, to still secure a spot on any team that will take me. Like you said, it's about confidence in yourself and abilities to get to the next level. That is a lesson I greatly value today and tell a lot of people I talk to in high school that want to go to perform athletically in college. To those in that position, never let anyone, including your doubts, keep you from doing what you want to do. author: @beniamincondrea5292
text: I just wanted to to share some of what I went through. I went to University of San Diego D1 running program. I lived in Oregon and wanted to experience life outside my comfort zone so I looked for colleges outside of my state. If you want to experience life outside of your comfort zone, try to contact coaches outside of your state during your Junior year of high school, because chances are the coaches won't see you. You can make phone calls with the coach and ask him specific questions like, "What times should I try to hit in the 3k, 8k, 1500m", "Is the school more focused more on distance running?", etc. Even better, visit the campus and participate in a training session to get a feel of how their training is like. Most coaches look for work ethic, and the difference in training will be significant from high school to college. Here's a perspective of how training was in college: 6:00AM - 9:00AM Morning speed work, 11:45AM - 12:30PM Weights/Dynamic Stretching, 5:00PM - 6:30PM OYO (on your own, usually 6-8 mile run).
